ingredients.name: String hopper flour (steamed/roasted rice flour, red or white)
ingredients.notes: use specific string hopper flour, not regular raw rice flour, for best texture

ingredients.name: Lukewarm water
ingredients.notes: may need slightly more depending on how dry the flour is

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: for greasing the string hopper trays

steps.instruction: Add the string hopper flour and salt to a bowl. Mix briefly with a wooden spoon.
Add the lukewarm water to the bowl little by little, mixing with the wooden spoon until the flour forms lumps of dough.

Mix the dough with your hand into one soft, pliable dough. It should be a little tacky but not sticky, holding its shape when squeezed without crumbling or sticking to your fingers. Adjust with a little more water if too dry, or a little more flour if too wet.
Lay out the string hopper trays and apply a thin coating of oil over their surface to prevent sticking.

Fill the string hopper press with dough, up to about 80% of its volume. Press the dough through the press onto each tray in a circular motion, covering the tray with strings, then cut the strings off with your finger.
Place the filled trays into the steamer basket, layering with minimal overlap for even steaming.
Steam for 5-6 minutes, or until the string hoppers are firm, springy to the touch, and not sticky.

Remove the trays from the steamer and gently lift the string hoppers off. Stack in a covered bowl to keep them from drying out while steaming the remaining batches. Serve warm with coconut sambol, dhal curry, or any preferred curry.

collection_method: scraped, single well-documented primary source written by a Sri Lankan home cook with precise gram measurements
notes: Known by many names across South Asia (idiyappam, nool puttu, noolappam, string hoppers); this entry reflects the Sri Lankan home-cooking method using a dedicated string hopper press and trays. A bamboo steamer basket with parchment paper can substitute for trays if unavailable. Quantities above make about 25-30 thick string hoppers, serving roughly 3 people as a main meal portion.
